questions.expl: Surface vibrators are effective only for shallow members up to about 200 mm thick, beyond which their vibration doesn't penetrate adequately.

questions.text: A surface vibrator for compacting of concrete is preferred for all the following except
questions.expl: Surface vibrators work well for shallow, wide elements like slabs, footings and pavements, but are not suitable for deep, narrow members like columns.

questions.text: Rational instability occurring during compaction of concrete using vibrations technique is due to
questions.expl: An oversanded mix has excess fines and reduced ability to allow entrapped air/water to escape during vibration, leading to instability.

questions.text: Maturity of concrete is the
options: Product of period of curing and temperature of curing
Percentage of strength of concrete cured at 18 C for 28 days
questions.expl: Maturity of concrete is a measure combining both the duration of curing and the curing temperature, since both jointly govern the degree of hydration achieved.

questions.text: The timber formwork for concrete should be made of
questions.expl: Timber formwork is generally made from well-seasoned soft wood planks, which are light, workable and economical.

questions.text: For a concrete slab for 3.75 x 4.75 m room, the stripping time of form should be
questions.expl: For a typical room-sized slab span, the formwork is generally kept in place for about 14 days before stripping, to allow adequate strength gain.

questions.text: To take care of any sag in the beams, the forms are given a camber of
questions.expl: Formwork for beams is typically given an upward camber of about 1:500 of the span to compensate for anticipated deflection/sag.

questions.text: For a medium income group big housing project which type of formwork is recommended?
questions.expl: Steel formwork, being durable and reusable many times, is the most economical choice for large housing projects with repetitive units.

questions.text: The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
questions.expl: Durability of concrete depends on its combined resistance to environmental deterioration, internal disruptive forces (like freeze-thaw or alkali-aggregate reaction) and chemical attack.

questions.text: The optimum number of revolutions over which concrete is required to be mixed in a mixer machine is
questions.expl: The optimum number of mixer revolutions for achieving a uniform, well-mixed batch is generally about 20.

questions.text: In hand mixed concrete, same strength of concrete can be achieved as that by concrete compacted with vibrator by
options: Cannot be achieved by any way
questions.expl: Since hand mixing traps more air and gives a less uniform mix than machine mixing, about 10% extra cement compensates for the resulting strength deficit.

questions.text: Steam curing, accelerates attainment of strength in concrete because
options: More water is available for curing
questions.expl: Steam curing raises the temperature of the concrete, speeding up the chemical hydration reaction and hence early strength gain.

questions.text: Steam curing should never be used for
questions.expl: High alumina cement is extremely heat-sensitive and can suffer a serious loss of strength ('conversion') if exposed to elevated curing temperatures, so steam curing must never be used with it.

questions.text: Curing of concrete at high temperature results in
questions.expl: Curing at elevated temperature accelerates hydration, giving earlier attainment of the ultimate strength than normal curing.

questions.text: Which factors comprise maturity of concrete?
options: Compressive strength and flexural strength of concrete
Cement content per cubic meter and compressive strength of concrete
Curing age and curing temperature of concrete
questions.expl: Maturity of concrete is calculated from the curing age combined with the curing temperature (typically as a time-temperature factor).

questions.text: When mixing water leaks out of the joints of shuttering, in which fresh concrete has been poured, the defect likely in cement concrete is
questions.expl: Water leaking out through gaps in the formwork carries fine material with it, leaving behind voids known as honeycombing.

questions.text: Weigh-batching proceeds on
options: The assumption of the declared weight in each bag of cement
Weighing the contents of each bag
Accurately estimating the weight of each material to be used in each batch
The assumption of correct dry weight of each size range of each material and the weight of water
questions.expl: Proper weigh-batching relies on accurately establishing the correct dry weight of each aggregate size fraction together with the water content, adjusting for moisture in the aggregates.

questions.text: Pick up the incorrect statement
options: About 10 percent more cement is consumed in making concrete if hand mixing is done
5 percent voids in cement concrete reduce strength up to 30 percent
Curing of OPC is done for 7 days
In high pressure steam curing, bond strength is increased
questions.expl: Contrary to the other (true) statements, high-pressure steam curing (autoclaving) is generally associated with a reduction, not an increase, in bond strength between concrete and reinforcement.

questions.text: In cold weather countries cement preferred is
questions.expl: In cold-weather regions, cement blended with calcium chloride (an accelerator) is preferred to speed up setting and hardening before frost can damage the fresh concrete.

questions.text: Workability of fibre reinforced concrete decreases, if
options: Fibre content and aspect ratio both are increased
Fibre content and aspect ratio both are decreased
Fibre content is increased and aspect ratio is decreased
Fibre content is decreased and aspect ratio is increased
questions.expl: Increasing both fibre content and aspect ratio raises internal friction and interlocking within the mix, reducing its workability.

questions.text: While concreting in cold weather where frosting is also likely, one uses
options: High quality Portland cement with minimum volume of added water
High alumina cement with calcium chloride additives
Portland cement together with calcium chloride additives
A mixture of high alumina cement and Portland cement
questions.expl: In frost-prone cold weather, high alumina cement (which hydrates and gains strength very rapidly, generating heat) combined with calcium chloride additives helps the concrete set and gain strength before freezing can occur.

questions.text: Which one of the following types of concrete is most suitable in extreme cold climates?
questions.expl: Ready-mix concrete, produced and quality-controlled at a central plant under controlled conditions, is generally the most practical and suitable choice for construction in extreme cold climates.
